title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: always-on diagnostics for macOS devices (roadmap phase 1)
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing, portal controls and troubleshooting constraints are supported. It accurately reports the disagreement between Microsoft's pages about macOS support and leaves the macOS default unstated rather than applying the documented Windows default.

claims.quote: Microsoft Purview compliance portal: Endpoint Data Loss Prevention -- Always-on diagnostics for macOS endpoints (Phase 1)

claims.claim: The roadmap plans automatic recording of comprehensive trace logs on onboarded Macs.
claims.quote: Comprehensive trace logs will be automatically recorded and stored locally on onboarded Mac devices

claims.claim: Learn describes Windows AOD traces as including policy-evaluation logs, classification results, enforcement actions and error states.
claims.quote: continuously collects Endpoint DLP trace logs in the background, such as policy-evaluation logs, classification results, enforcement actions, and error states.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The Microsoft pages do not describe the specific contents of macOS AOD trace logs.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Always-on diagnostics macOS default enabled automatically trace log contents macOS specific storage settings. Read AOD feature page and Paste troubleshooting page; the latter describes trace contents but explicitly confines AOD support to Windows.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Scoped Purview administrators are not supported for the documented diagnostics permissions.

claims.claim: Trace recording is continuous once Always-on diagnostics is enabled.
claims.quote: The Always-on diagnostics feature in Microsoft Purview enables continuous, automated trace logging for endpoint data loss prevention (DLP).

claims.claim: The documented support workflow has Microsoft Support request traces and the customer administrator collect them from the affected device.
claims.quote: Microsoft Support requests diagnostic trace logs, which the customer administrator collects from the affected device using documented procedures.
